q: A bank is moving sensitive data to the public cloud. The regulator requires that the bank be able at any moment to prevent the provider from accessing plaintext data, and that the key material never be in the provider's possession. Which key management model BEST meets the requirement?
options: Provider-managed keys with automatic rotation
A customer-managed key generated in the provider's KMS
Hold Your Own Key (an external key store in the bank's HSM)
Bring Your Own Key imported into the provider's KMS
explain: Only HYOK/an external key store keeps the key material exclusively with the customer. With BYOK the key is generated by the customer but imported into the provider's KMS, so a copy is in the provider's possession. CMK and provider-managed keys are created at the provider.

q: An organization is terminating its contract with an IaaS provider and must ensure that the data on volumes and in backups at the provider cannot be recovered. All data has been encrypted from the start with customer-managed keys. Which method is BEST?
options: Destroy the keys (cryptographic erase) and document the destruction
Ask the provider to degauss the disks
Overwrite the volumes with zeros three times before deletion
Delete the volumes and backups through the console
explain: Crypto-shredding is a method the customer controls and it also covers replicas and backups, provided the data was encrypted from the start. Overwriting does not guarantee erasure of physical blocks (SSDs, replicas), degaussing is not feasible in a multi-tenant environment, and ordinary deletion leaves the data recoverable.

q: An application on a virtual machine needs to read objects from the same provider's storage service. Which approach is BEST?
options: An administrator user's access key in a configuration file
Assign the VM a role (managed identity) with minimal read permissions for that bucket
A dedicated service user's access key, encrypted and rotated every 90 days
Public access to the bucket restricted to the VM's IP address
explain: For service access, workload identities with automatically rotated temporary credentials and least privilege are best. Static keys, even rotated ones, can leak, and a public bucket with an IP filter is not an identity control.

q: Cloud administrators have permanent global administrator rights. Which measure MOST reduces the risk of abuse or compromise of these accounts?
options: Longer passwords changed every 30 days
A quarterly review of the administrator list
Prohibiting console access outside business hours
Privileged Access Management with just-in-time assignment, phishing-resistant MFA and session recording
explain: PAM with JIT access removes standing privileges, while phishing-resistant MFA and session recording add prevention and accountability. The other measures help, but do not remove the permanent exposure of privileged accounts.

q: Due to regulation, European clients' data may exist only in EU regions, and sign-ins to the administrative console should be allowed only from countries where the company operates. Which concept covers both controls?
options: Microsegmentation
Traffic inspection
Geofencing
Network security groups
explain: Geofencing restricts operation or access by geographic location: both the location of resources (allowed regions) and the location of sign-ins. It should be used together with IAM and MFA because IP location can be spoofed with a VPN.

q: The incident response team cannot analyze a compromised container because the orchestrator has already replaced the pod with a new one. What is the BEST measure for the future?
options: Disable auto-scaling and automatic pod replacement
Move all workloads to long-lived virtual machines
Give developers SSH access to all nodes
Send logs and runtime telemetry centrally and immediately to immutable storage, with automated evidence collection
explain: Ephemeral resources are a security advantage, so they should not be abolished. The solution is for evidence not to live on the resource: centralized logging, runtime telemetry and automated snapshot/isolation before shutdown.

q: According to CSA threat reports and incident analyses, what is the MOST COMMON cause of data leaks from public cloud storage?
options: Misconfiguration by the customer
A breach of the provider's hypervisor
Quantum attacks on encryption
Physical theft of disks from the data center
explain: Misconfiguration (public buckets, overly broad permissions, open ports) is consistently the main cause of incidents. Breaches of the provider's infrastructure and physical theft are rare.

q: A team is moving to an immutable architecture. How is a critical OS security patch applied in this model?
options: An administrator logs in to each server and installs the patch
A new golden image with the patch is built, tested and the existing instances are replaced
A configuration tool automatically installs the patch on live servers
The patch is postponed until the next quarterly window
explain: In an immutable architecture live servers are not changed. A change means a new image and replacement of instances (rolling or blue/green), which eliminates configuration drift and enables fast rollback.

q: The security team wants to detect deviations of virtual machine configurations from the approved secure state. What must exist FIRST?
options: An IDS on every subnet
A penetration test of all machines
A documented security baseline (e.g., based on a CIS Benchmark)
Automatic shutdown of non-compliant machines
explain: Drift can only be measured against a reference. The baseline defines the approved state; only then can tools detect and correct deviations.

q: In a public IaaS cloud, who is responsible for the security and patching of the hypervisor?
options: The customer, for each VM it runs
The cloud broker
The customer and the provider equally
The cloud service provider
explain: The hypervisor and physical infrastructure are below the customer's responsibility boundary in all service models. The customer verifies this through audit reports (SOC 2, ISO 27001), not by managing it itself.

q: Management requests a DR solution for a new cloud system. The team proposes multi-region active/active. What should the security manager do FIRST?
options: Approve the proposal because it provides the lowest RTO
Conduct a Business Impact Analysis to determine the MTD, RTO and RPO
Test failover between regions
Negotiate a discount with the provider for the second region
explain: The BIA determines recovery requirements and process criticality. Without it, it is unknown whether the expensive active/active strategy is justified (CBA) or whether warm standby or backup and restore is sufficient.

q: The BIA showed that the reporting system can be unavailable for 3 days and that the acceptable data loss is 24 hours. Which DR strategy is MOST APPROPRIATE?
options: Backup and restore to another region
Warm standby
Multi-site active/active
Pilot light with synchronous replication
explain: A loose RTO and RPO justify the cheapest strategy. More expensive options would violate the principle that the cost of a control must not exceed its benefit.

q: How must the RTO and MTD relate for a critical process?
options: The RTO must equal the RPO
The RTO must be greater than the MTD to provide a margin
The RTO must be less than the MTD
They are unrelated; the MTD applies only to data
explain: The MTD is the limit beyond which irreparable harm occurs; the RTO is the recovery objective and must be shorter than the MTD, allowing time for verification. The RPO measures acceptable data loss, not recovery time.

q: During an emergency the business can operate at 50% of its usual processing capacity. Which metric describes this?
options: Recovery Point Objective
Recovery Service Level
Maximum Tolerable Downtime
Annualized Rate of Occurrence
explain: The RSL is the percentage of normal service capacity required during recovery or an emergency. It directly affects the size of the DR environment and the cost.

q: A ransomware protection control costs €80,000 per year. The expected annual loss without it is €60,000, and with it €10,000. What does the cost-benefit analysis show?
options: The control is justified because it reduces risk by 83%
The control is justified because ransomware is a critical threat
The control is neutral because the ROI is exactly zero
The control is not economically justified because it costs more than the loss reduction (€50,000)
explain: The benefit is 60,000 − 10,000 = €50,000 per year and the cost €80,000, so the ROI is negative. A cheaper control or a different risk treatment should be sought.

q: An architect wants an application to be able to move to another provider with minimal changes. Which design BEST supports this functional requirement?
options: A containerized application on Kubernetes, IaC and data in open formats
Using as many proprietary serverless services of one provider as possible
A longer contract with the current provider for better prices
Manual installation on virtual machines according to internal documentation
explain: Portability is achieved through abstraction from the provider and standard formats. Proprietary services and long contracts increase vendor lock-in, and manual installation makes repeatable moves harder.

q: An organization uses SaaS for human resources. Where should it focus the MOST security effort?
options: Provider assessment and the contract, IAM with SSO and MFA, sharing configuration and data export
Patching the database behind the application
Hardening the operating system of the application servers
Configuring security groups in front of the application
explain: In SaaS the customer does not manage the OS, database or network. Its main tools are the provider assessment (SOC 2, contract), IAM and tenant configuration.

q: Which framework uses pillars such as security, reliability, operational excellence, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability to evaluate a cloud architecture?
options: CSA Cloud Controls Matrix
Well-Architected Framework
NIST SP 800-88
SANS security principles
explain: The Well-Architected Framework (AWS, and similarly Azure and Google) organizes best practices into pillars. The CCM is a control catalog, NIST SP 800-88 deals with sanitization, and the SANS principles are general design principles.

q: A developer accidentally pushed production cloud credentials to a public repository. What should be done FIRST?
options: Remove the commit from the repository history
Add secret scanning to the CI pipeline
Revoke and rotate the credentials
Report the incident to the provider and wait for instructions
explain: Credentials must be considered compromised as soon as they are public; they are revoked first, then the logs are analyzed for abuse. Rewriting history does not help because they may already have been copied, and secret scanning is a preventive measure for the future.

q: Which statement BEST describes the secure by design principle as promoted by CISA and its partners?
options: The customer is responsible for hardening the product itself according to the manufacturer's instructions
Security is tested only after delivery, through a bug bounty
Security features are offered as a paid add-on
The manufacturer takes ownership of security, with secure default settings and the elimination of vulnerability classes from the start
explain: Secure by design shifts the burden to the manufacturer: secure by default, MFA and logging at no extra cost, memory-safe languages and eliminating entire classes of vulnerabilities during design, not after the fact.

q: Order the cloud BC/DR planning activities from first to last.
options: Choose a DR strategy (e.g., warm standby) based on the RTO/RPO and CBA
Test the plan (tabletop, then a parallel test) and update it
Conduct a BIA and determine the MTD, RTO and RPO for critical processes
Define the scope of the plan and obtain management support
Implement replication, backups and IaC for the DR region
explain: Planning starts with scope and management support, then the BIA provides the requirements, from which the strategy is chosen, then it is implemented, and finally tested and maintained.

q: Match the scenario with the MOST APPROPRIATE method or control.
options: The customer is leaving the public cloud and wants encrypted data to be unrecoverable.
The CSP is retiring magnetic tapes in the data center.
Stateful traffic filtering for an individual virtual machine.
Analyzing traffic between VPCs to detect attacks.
Preventing configuration drift on production servers.
targets: Traffic inspection (IDS/IPS in an inspection VPC)
explain: The customer uses crypto-shredding, the CSP can degauss magnetic media, an NSG is a stateful per-instance filter, an IDS/IPS performs traffic inspection, and an immutable architecture eliminates drift. Geofencing is a distractor.
